title: Bidirectional A* Conquers Porto Foz Faster!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* race from both ends across a real street grid in Porto (Foz do Douro). The visualization highlights how two guided searches meet to drastically cut explored nodes.
ig_caption:
🧭⚡ **Bidirectional A*** is like running two detectives at once—one from the start and one from the goal. Instead of searching blindly across a graph, we perform **two coordinated A*** frontiers that expand using a heuristic, then **terminate when the searches meet**—often reducing work compared to single-direction search.

📍On a real street-map graph of **Porto (Foz do Douro)**, intersections become **nodes** and road segments become **weighted edges**. Because heuristics estimate remaining cost (via shortest-path intuition), Bidirectional A* balances **optimality guarantees** (when set up consistently) with **high efficiency**—a true graph-theory win for shortest-path routing.

🎥 Want to see this on *your* city or a custom route? Comment the neighborhood + start/end pins and I’ll generate the next visualization! 👇
fb_caption:
🗺️ **Graph Search, But Smarter:** In this visualization of **Bidirectional A***, we search from both the start and the goal simultaneously using heuristics to guide expansion. On a real street-map graph (intersections as nodes, roads as weighted edges), the two frontiers meet sooner—often exploring far fewer possibilities than one-way search.
